name: Electric standing desk
tagline: A motorised steel frame that you build upside down, then flip. Heavy, but genuinely simple.
covers: Standing desk frames bought without a top
peopleNote: Two people for the flip. The frame alone can weigh seventy pounds.

tools.n: Cordless drill with a Phillips bit
tools.why: Driving twenty-plus wood screws into the top. Doing this by hand is genuinely miserable.
Centring the frame on the top.
Marking screw positions if your top is not pre-drilled.

before: Clear a big floor area. You build the whole thing upside down and then flip it.
Put the top face-down on its own packaging. Standing desk tops are often bamboo or laminate and scratch instantly.
Check whether your top is pre-drilled. If not, you will be marking and drilling pilot holes, which adds twenty minutes.
Have the power outlet location in mind. The control box cable is not long.
safety: Never put your fingers between the legs and the frame while the desk is powering. The motors have real force.
Keep cables clear of the lifting columns. A cable caught in a rising desk will be pulled apart.
Do not exceed the stated weight limit, and remember a loaded desk raising itself puts all that weight on the motors.

steps.title: Top face-down, frame parts laid out around it
steps.say: Lay the desktop upside down on its packaging. Put the two leg columns, the crossbar, and the feet around it in roughly the right positions.
do: Top face-down on padding
Two leg columns, two feet, one crossbar
Hardware bag opened into a bowl

steps.title: Bolt the crossbar to the leg columns
steps.say: The telescoping crossbar connects the two leg columns. Bolt it to both, finger-tight, and leave it loose so you can set the width later.
do: Crossbar brackets onto the columns
Finger-tight only
If the crossbar is adjustable, leave its width bolts loose too
steps.tip: The crossbar usually adjusts in length to match different desktop widths. Setting it before you know your top width is backwards.

steps.title: Bolt the feet onto the columns
steps.say: Each foot bolts to the bottom of a leg column. Note which way the foot points — the longer side usually goes toward the front of the desk.
do: Foot plate onto the column base
All bolts started, then tightened firmly
Check both feet point the same way
steps.watch: Feet on backwards makes the desk unstable front to back, which you only notice when you lean on it. Compare both sides.

steps.title: Center the frame on the top and set the crossbar width
steps.say: Measure so the frame is centered side to side and set back a little from the front edge. Then tighten the crossbar width bolts.
do: Measure from each side edge to the frame — make the numbers equal
Set the frame back about an inch from the front edge
Now tighten the crossbar length bolts
steps.tip: Setting the frame slightly back from the front edge means the front edge sits comfortably against you rather than over the steel.
steps.watch: An off-center frame makes the desk sag on the long side and look crooked. Measure both sides before you drive a single screw.

steps.title: Screw the frame to the top
steps.say: Drive the wood screws through the frame into the top. If the top is not pre-drilled, mark every hole and drill shallow pilot holes first.
do: Use only the short screws for the top
Pre-drilled top: straight in
Undrilled top: mark, then pilot drill to about two thirds of the screw length
steps.watch: Screw length matters enormously here. A long screw through a three-quarter inch top comes out the other side, and that is permanent damage to a desk you cannot hide.
steps.tip: If you are using a drill, set the clutch low. These are chipboard or bamboo tops and they strip easily.

steps.title: Mount the control box and keypad
steps.say: The control box screws under the top, usually near the center. The keypad goes on the front edge on your dominant side.
do: Control box in the center underside, away from the lifting columns
Keypad on the front edge, right side for most people
Pre-drill if your top is hardwood or bamboo
steps.tip: Sit in your chair and reach for where the keypad should be before you screw it down. Most people mount it too far in.

steps.title: Plug in the motor cables and tidy them
steps.say: Each leg's motor cable plugs into the control box, plus the keypad and the power. Then clip every cable into the tray with plenty of slack.
do: Each motor cable into its labelled port
Keypad cable and power cable in
Clip all cables away from the lifting columns, with slack for full travel
steps.watch: Leave enough slack for the desk at full height. A cable that is just long enough at sitting height will be ripped out the first time it rises.

steps.title: Flip it with help
steps.say: Two people, lift by the frame and the top together, and set it down on its feet. Do not lever it over on the legs.
do: One person each end
Lift, do not roll
Set down on all feet at once
steps.watch: Rolling a standing desk over on one leg puts the entire weight through a lifting column sideways. That is how motors get damaged.

steps.title: Reset the desk before you use it
steps.say: Almost every electric desk needs an initialization reset. Hold the down button until it drops, bounces, and beeps. Until you do this, it may not move at all.
do: Plug in
Hold the down arrow for about ten seconds
The desk lowers, dips, and beeps or flashes — that is the reset
steps.tip: If a brand new standing desk 'does not work', this reset is the answer about four times out of five. It is in the manual, usually on the last page.

steps.title: Set your heights and save presets
steps.say: Sitting height: elbows level with the top, feet flat. Standing height: same elbow rule. Save both as presets.
do: Sit, adjust until elbows are level with the desk surface
Save as preset one
Stand, repeat, save as preset two
steps.tip: Monitor top at or just below eye level. Most people set a standing desk slightly too low and then lean.

fixes.q: The desk does not move at all
fixes.a: Do the initialization reset: hold the down button for about ten seconds until the desk drops slightly and beeps. This is required on a new desk and is the most common 'faulty desk' that is not faulty.

fixes.q: It makes a beeping error code
fixes.a: Look the code up in the manual — usually it means one motor cable is not fully seated, or the legs are out of sync. Unplug, reseat both motor cables, plug in, and reset.

fixes.q: One side rises faster than the other
fixes.a: The legs are out of sync. Run the reset procedure, which re-zeroes both motors together.

fixes.q: A screw came through the desktop
fixes.a: Wrong screw length. Back it out, fill with a wax repair stick in a matching color, and use the short screws. Compare screw length to top thickness before driving any others.

fixes.q: The desk wobbles at standing height
fixes.a: Some wobble at full extension is normal for single-motor frames. Check the crossbar bolts and foot bolts are fully tight, make sure the frame is centered, and avoid leaning on the far corner.

fixes.q: A cable got pulled out when it raised
fixes.a: Not enough slack. Unclip the cables, raise the desk to full height, then re-clip with the cables relaxed at that height.
